paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Tom, Lily, and Mia were at the bus station in the town. The bus station was big, and many people were there. They wanted to go to Green Hill to see Grandma and Grandpa. Mia's mom said yes, and Tom looked after the girls. Tom was the oldest, so he asked for the information. "Excuse me," said Tom to a woman at the information desk. "Where is the bus to Green Hill?" "It is at stop two," said the woman. "It goes at nine o'clock." "Thank you," said Tom.

At stop two, an old yellow bus was waiting. The driver called, "Passengers for Green Hill, please get on!" The three children got on the bus. Many other passengers sat in the bus. "Listen to the engine!" said Lily. "It is very loud," said Mia. "It is old, and the engine is weak," said Tom. "It goes slowly up the hill." Mia sat next to the window.

"How long is the ride?" asked Lily. "It is forty minutes," said Tom. "Forty minutes is only a little," said Lily. "I think a long ride is boring," said Mia. "Not today," said Lily. "Look at the river and the green hills." Mia had a bag with water and fruit. She looked out of the window and smiled.

At twenty to ten, the bus stopped in Green Hill. Grandma and Grandpa were waiting at the bus stop. "Here are my three passengers!" said Grandpa. "Welcome to Green Hill." Lily laughed and ran to Grandma. "The ride was not boring at all," she said.
text.summary: Tom, Lily, and Mia ride the bus from the town to Green Hill. They ask for information, talk about the old bus, and meet Grandma and Grandpa.
